text: Selling currency into a reserve when price is above the peg and buying it back with the reserve when price is below the peg yields an arbitrage profit, so a reserve can fund its own defense of the peg.
citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vadhindran K. Rao, Stable Cryptocurrencies - First Order Principles (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3402701
abstract: In the next paragraph we demonstrate the obvious result that selling the currency when the price is high to build a reserve, then buying the currency back with the reserve when the price is low will yield an arbitrage profit

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: the reserve currency is more stable than the base currency
the cost to implement and maintain the reserve is ignored
